newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends up 8.92 pct on bullish mood.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends up 8.92 pct on bullish mood.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B share index ended up 8.92 percent on Friday on bullish sentiment with both overseas institutions and domestic investors buying actively, brokers said.
However, some profit-taking emerged in the afternoon session, pushing the index off its intraday high of 88.133 points, they said.
The B index surged 7.180 points to close at 87.676, with turnover hitting a record high of $65.159 million, compared with $23.748 million on Thursday, brokers said.
"Market sentiment was bullish with huge inflows of fresh capital entering the market, indicating that there is still further room for rises in the short term," one broker said.
"Both domestic and overseas institutions were seen building positions, so the upward trend could last for weeks," another broker said.

Brokers said Beijing's move on Friday to return control of the stock markets to the central government had little impact on trading because the action had already been factored into the market following long-running rumours.
China announced on Friday that the State Council had decided to put the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges under direct control of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, China's market watchdog.
All 47 B shares traded, with 46 up and one flat.
Shanghai Diesel Engine was the star B share, rising $0.030 or 10.13 percent to $0.326.
Property developer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development Co was the most actively traded B share, jumping $0.116 or 10.03 percent to $1.272 on volume of around 10.3 million shares.
Domestic currency A shares fell as investors unwound their positions before the weekend, and the index was expected to move in a narrow range in the short term, brokers said.
The A index slipped 30.109 points or 2.47 percent to 1,188.824 points on turnover of 3.287 billion yuan against 3.402 billion on Thursday.
The SSE30 blue chip index fell 85.817 points or 2.34 percent to 3,579.910 points.
Sichuan Electrical Apparatus Co was the worst performer, plunging 0.76 yuan or 9.93 percent to 6.89 yuan.
Brokers were uncertain about the direction of the B share index on Monday, saying some profit-taking was possible but foreign funds were likely to continue to enter the market.
"If foreign investors take a rest and domestic investors take profit, the bullish mood is likely to be hurt," said one broker.
"But if foreign investors continue to rush to the Shanghai market, the index is likely to move higher," he said.
